chapter: Ben Pollack band and New York
title: Glenn Miller on the tennis court; Miller's background
summary: He wins a dollar a game from the competitive Miller, and describes Miller's musical background.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: I was speaking about Glen what Miller and a very interesting guy he was. And I said he was a task master. And he was also a very competitive guy. I know later on I used to play tennis with him down in New Orleans. And he was an excellent tennis player. And believe me, I was nothing on tennis. You know mediocre, very mediocre. But Glen would like to smash that ball. This was the kind of, his character you know. He wanted to hit that ball hard and smash it over so you couldn't even get

close to it.
So he kept trying that on me and I said, want to play a dollar a game? And he said, certainly. (LAUGHTER). Well certainly you know, and I know he could have beat me. So us said, well give us some incentive. And we played a dollar a game and he didn't win one game. (LAUGHTER). He didn't win game number one. He would get madder and madder and he'd smash that ball so hard and it keep going into the net or it would go over the line. And I think I won, oh I don't know, ten or eleven dollars from him. (LAUGHTER).
So anyway, that's the type of person he was.
He was, as I say, ....
What kind of musical background did he have?

Oh he came from Boulder, Colorado and went to the, I guess, the University of Colorado. And that's where he met his wife, Helen. And he was a bandsman. He was a bandsman. He was not a very good improvisor, a good jazz musician. And he was first influenced by Miff Mole on the trombone. But he was an excellent musician. A great arranger and he played his horn very well. I mean he played legitimate things
beautifully. A good reader, good execution. Great facility on his instrument. Good tone and I think a dedicated musician you know.
